title: J. van Zuylen (1981) The microscopes of Antoni van Leeuwenhoek (Journal of Microscopy 121)
facts: Table 1: nine Leeuwenhoek microscopes; Utrecht lens magnification 266, numerical aperture 0.37, measured resolving power 1.35 um
measured resolving powers of the other instruments 2 to 4 um (e.g. 2.3, 3.3, 4, 2, 3.5, 3.0); numerical apertures 0.11 to 0.32
Utrecht: resolving power measured by Harting (1850) and Van Cittert (1932-34) 1.42 um with the same Nobert test plate; the author found 1.35 um photographing diatoms
1825: Joseph Jackson Lister develops combined lenses that cancelled spherical and chromatic aberration
1860s: Abbe sine condition; microscope design until then largely based on trial and error
objective numerical aperture ranges from 0.14 to 0.7 (typical dry objectives); oil immersion up to about 1.5-1.6
